chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from Abū Baṣīr said:

I said to Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, indeed these two companions of mine were ignorant that they did not stand at al-Muzdalifah.' He said, 'They return to their place and stand at al-Mash'ar for an hour.' I said, 'Indeed no one informed them, until it was the day when the people had departed.' He lowered his head for a moment, then said, 'Did they not pray the morning prayer at al-Muzdalifah?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Did they not make qunut in their prayer?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Their Hajj is complete.' Then he said, 'Al-Mash'ar is part of al-Muzdalifah, and al-Muzdalifah is part of al-Mash'ar, and indeed a little supplication suffices for them.'

key_terms.الْمَشْعَر: Al-Mash'ar, referring to the Monument (Jamarat) area, considered part of Muzdalifah
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Muzdalifah, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims gather after leaving Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to stand at Muzdalifah during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of the *wuquf* (standing) at al-Muzdalifah, ruling that a brief pause suffices if the pilgrims have already prayed the morning prayer there. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that al-Mash'ar al-Muqaddas and al-Muzdalifah are not strictly distinct locations but rather part of a single continuous space, thereby easing the burden on pilgrims who may have missed the specific ritual stand due to forgetfulness or necessity.
